title: Poverty made a pretext for mockery
literal_meaning: A poor man’s wife is everyone’s sister-in-law (wife’s sister).
meaning_odia: ଗରିବ ଲୋକର ସ୍ତ୍ରୀକୁ ସମସ୍ତେ ନିଜ ଶାଳୀ ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବାର ରୂପକ ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟର ସୁଯୋଗ ନେଇ ଲୋକେ ଥଟ୍ଟା ପରିହାସ କରନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ଅସମ୍ମାନ ଓ ଅନଧିକାର ଘନିଷ୍ଠତାର ଛବି; ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟ କାହାର ସମ୍ମାନ କମାଏ ନାହିଁ।
explanation: The saying makes an impossible family claim: everyone treats the poor man’s wife as their own sister-in-law. The inspected gloss explains this as taking advantage of poverty to mock people. Our reading focuses on the disrespect in that claimed familiarity, rather than treating poverty as a reason anyone deserves it.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A discussion turns to people who ridicule a neighbour because the household has little money. Someone cites the proverb as a sharp image of that disrespect and challenges the mockery.
cultural_context: The kinship word ଶାଳୀ supplies a claim of personal familiarity, while ସବୁରି expands that claim to everyone. The source gloss links this intrusion to poverty. The woman in the image carries the insult directed at a household’s vulnerable position.

witnesses.locator: Page14, third item beginning ଗରିବ ମାଇପ.
